question: What could a smartwatch notice, days before people with COVID-19 felt ill?
answer: A rise in resting heart rate. Mishra's team analysed smartwatch data and found an unusual climb in resting pulse in most infected wearers, at or before the first symptoms; an alert system could have flagged 63% of cases in advance. The body fights an infection before it tells its owner.
move: A rise against a person's own baseline says more than any population average.
ask: Do I know my own normal well enough to notice when something starts to drift?
source: Mishra et al., Nature Biomedical Engineering, 2020
